Let $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ with
$g[A] \subseteq B$ and let $f : B \to \mathbb{R}$, so that the composite
$f \circ g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ is defined. Let $c \in A$ be a limit point of
$A$ ([[def-limit-point-r]]) at which $g$ is differentiable
([[def-derivative]]), put $b := g(c)$, and suppose $b$ is a limit point of $B$
at which $f$ is differentiable. Then $f \circ g$ is differentiable at $c$ and

$$(f \circ g)'(c) \;=\; f'\bigl(g(c)\bigr)\,g'(c) .$$

**Both limit-point hypotheses are needed, and neither is automatic.** That $c$
is a limit point of $A$ is what makes $g'(c)$ and $(f \circ g)'(c)$ defined
symbols; that $b = g(c)$ is a limit point of $B$ is what makes $f'(b)$ one.
Nothing forces the second: $g$ may be differentiable at $c$ and send $c$ to an
isolated point of $B$, and there $f'(b)$ is not defined and the formula asserts
nothing.

**No case analysis appears anywhere.** The naive difference-quotient proof
writes $\frac{f(g(x)) - f(g(c))}{g(x) - g(c)} \cdot \frac{g(x) - g(c)}{x - c}$
and then has to say what happens where $g(x) = g(c)$, which may occur at points
arbitrarily close to $c$. Carathéodory's factorisation never divides by the
inner increment, so the difficulty does not arise.

Throughout, $\mathbb{R}$ is the complete ordered field
([[def-complete-ordered-field]]), neighbourhoods are those of
[[def-neighbourhood-r]] and limit points those of [[def-limit-point-r]].

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $c \in A$ be a
**limit point of $A$**. The **difference quotient of $f$ at $c$** is the function

$$q_{f,c} : A \setminus \{c\} \to \mathbb{R}, \qquad q_{f,c}(x) := \frac{f(x) - f(c)}{x - c} .$$

The division is legitimate at every point of the domain, since $x \ne c$ gives
$x - c \ne 0$.

**The point $c$ is a limit point of $A \setminus \{c\}$, not merely of $A$.**
For every real $\varepsilon > 0$ the punctured neighbourhood
$N^{*}_{\varepsilon}(c)$ omits $c$, so

$$N^{*}_{\varepsilon}(c) \cap A \;=\; N^{*}_{\varepsilon}(c) \cap (A \setminus \{c\}) ,$$

and the left-hand side is nonempty because $c$ is a limit point of $A$. So
$q_{f,c}$ is a function on a set having $c$ as a limit point, and
$\lim_{x \to c} q_{f,c}(x)$ is a notion that [[def-function-limit]] defines.

$f$ is **differentiable at $c$** when that limit exists, and then the
**derivative of $f$ at $c$** is

$$f'(c) \;:=\; \lim_{x \to c} q_{f,c}(x) \;=\; \lim_{x \to c} \frac{f(x) - f(c)}{x - c} .$$

**Two obligations are carried by that notation, and both are discharged here.**

1. **Uniqueness.** Writing $f'(c)$ treats the right-hand side as a name for a
   single real number. That is legitimate: $c$ is a limit point of the domain
   $A \setminus \{c\}$ of $q_{f,c}$, so at most one real can satisfy the
   $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ condition, by [[lem-function-limit-unique]] applied to
   $q_{f,c}$. Two reals both meeting the condition are therefore equal, and the
   symbol denotes.
2. **Meaningfulness.** The hypothesis that $c$ is a limit point of $A$ is not
   decoration. At an **isolated** point of $A$ the punctured condition
   $0 < |x - c| < \delta$ is met by no point of the domain at all, so the
   $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ formula is satisfied vacuously by *every* real at
   once; this is why [[def-function-limit]] leaves the limit undefined there,
   and it is why this library defines $f'(c)$ only at a limit point of $A$. At
   an isolated point of its domain a function is neither differentiable nor
   non-differentiable here: the question is not posed.

**The limit sees only $A \setminus \{c\}$, so how the difference quotient is
extended to $c$ is irrelevant.** Let $Q : A \to \mathbb{R}$ agree with
$q_{f,c}$ at every point of $A \setminus \{c\}$, and let $L \in \mathbb{R}$.
Then $\lim_{x \to c} Q(x) = L$ if and only if $\lim_{x \to c} q_{f,c}(x) = L$.
Both conditions read: for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a real
$\delta > 0$ such that every point $x$ of the relevant domain with
$0 < |x - c| < \delta$ satisfies $|{\cdot} - L| < \varepsilon$
([[def-function-limit]]). The clause $0 < |x - c|$ removes $x = c$ from both
quantifiers, so in both cases the points quantified over are exactly the
$x \in A \setminus \{c\}$ with $0 < |x - c| < \delta$, at which $Q$ and
$q_{f,c}$ take the same value. The two conditions are the same condition.

**Differentiability on a set.** For $S \subseteq A$, $f$ is **differentiable on
$S$** when it is differentiable at every $c \in S$; implicit in that phrase is
that every point of $S$ is a limit point of $A$. $f$ is **differentiable** when
it is differentiable on the whole of $A$.

**Restriction of the domain.** Let $B \subseteq A$, let $c \in B$ and suppose
$c$ is a limit point of $B$. If $f$ is differentiable at $c$, then so is the
restriction $f|_B : B \to \mathbb{R}$, and

$$(f|_B)'(c) \;=\; f'(c) .$$

Indeed $B \setminus \{c\} \subseteq A \setminus \{c\}$; the displayed identity
of punctured neighbourhoods above, applied to $B$, shows that $c$ is a limit
point of $B \setminus \{c\}$; the difference quotient $q_{f|_B, c}$ is the
restriction of $q_{f,c}$ to $B \setminus \{c\}$, since $f|_B(c) = f(c)$; and
claim 2 of [[lem-limit-is-local]] carries the limit to that restriction.

**Every point of a nondegenerate interval is a limit point of it.** Let
$J \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be order-convex ([[def-interval]]) with at least two
elements and let $p \in J$. Choose $q \in J$ with $q \ne p$, and let a real
$\varepsilon > 0$ be given. If $p < q$, put $y := p + \tfrac{1}{2}\min\{\varepsilon,\ q - p\}$;
then $p < y$, and $y - p \le \tfrac{1}{2}(q-p) < q - p$, so $p < y < q$ and
order-convexity gives $y \in J$, while $0 < |y - p| < \varepsilon$. If $q < p$,
the point $y := p - \tfrac{1}{2}\min\{\varepsilon,\ p - q\}$ serves in the same
way. So $N^{*}_{\varepsilon}(p) \cap J \ne \varnothing$ for every real
$\varepsilon > 0$, that is, $p$ is a limit point of $J$
([[def-limit-point-r]]).

Consequently, for $f$ defined on a nondegenerate interval $I$, the symbol
$f'(c)$ is meaningful at **every** $c \in I$, endpoints included. At an endpoint
the difference quotient is taken over the points of $I$ lying on the one side
that is available, so what other texts call a one-sided derivative is, here,
simply the derivative of $f$ on $I$.

Let $a<b$, let $\varphi$ be $C^1$ and injective on a neighborhood of $[a,b]$, and suppose $\varphi'(x)\ne0$ there. If $f$ is continuous on an interval containing $\varphi([a,b])$, then
$$\int_{\min\{\varphi(a),\varphi(b)\}}^{\max\{\varphi(a),\varphi(b)\}}f(y)\,dy=\int_a^b f(\varphi(x))|\varphi'(x)|\,dx.$$
Thus the absolute derivative is the correct factor for the unoriented image interval.

derivations.claim: [Second derivatives under the substitution] Since $\xi\mapsto\ell\xi$ is $C^1$ with derivative $\ell$ and inverse $x\mapsto x/\ell$, the map $\psi=u\circ(\cdot/\ell)$ is $C^2$ exactly when $u$ is, and by [F1] applied twice, $$\psi'(x)=\frac{u'(x/\ell)}{\ell},\qquad \psi''(x)=\frac{u''(x/\ell)}{\ell^{2}}\qquad(x\in\ell I).$$
[The scale identity] From the definition of $h$ and $W$, $E_\star>0$, $$h^{2}=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m\ell^{2}E_\star},\qquad\text{hence}\qquad \frac{1}{h^{2}\ell^{2}}=\frac{2mE_\star}{\hbar^{2}} .$$

[Forward implication of (a)] Suppose $u$ is $C^2$ with $u''=(W-\lambda)u/h^{2}$ on $I$. By step 1.1, $\psi$ is $C^2$ on $\ell I$ and $$\psi''(x)=\frac{u''(x/\ell)}{\ell^{2}} =\frac{1}{\ell^{2}}\cdot\frac{W(x/\ell)-\lambda}{h^{2}}\,u(x/\ell) =\frac{2mE_\star}{\hbar^{2}}\bigl(W(x/\ell)-\lambda\bigr)\psi(x),$$ by step 1.2. Multiplying by $-\hbar^{2}/(2m)$ and bringing $\psi$ terms to the left gives $-(\hbar^{2}/2m)\psi''+E_\star W(x/\ell)\psi=E_\star\lambda\psi$ on $\ell I$.

[Converse implication of (a)] Suppose conversely that $\psi$ is $C^2$ with $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\psi''+E_\star W(x/\ell)\psi=E_\star\lambda\psi$ on $\ell I$. By step 1.1, $u(\xi)=\psi(\ell\xi)$ is $C^2$ on $I$ with $u''(\xi)=\ell^{2}\psi''(\ell\xi)$; substituting the assumed equation at $x=\ell\xi$ gives $$u''(\xi)=\ell^{2}\cdot\frac{2m}{\hbar^{2}}\bigl(E_\star W(\xi)-E_\star\lambda\bigr)\psi(\ell\xi) =\frac{2m\ell^{2}E_\star}{\hbar^{2}}\bigl(W(\xi)-\lambda\bigr)u(\xi) =\frac{W(\xi)-\lambda}{h^{2}}u(\xi),$$ the last equality by step 1.2.

[The exponent identity (b)] On $[a,b]$ the function $x\mapsto\ell x$ is $C^1$ and strictly increasing with derivative $\ell>0$, and the integrand $f(x):=\sqrt{2m(E_\star W(x/\ell)-E_\star\lambda)}$ is continuous on $[\ell a,\ell b]$ because $W$ is continuous and $W-\lambda>0$. By [F2] applied to $\varphi(\xi)=\ell\xi$, $$\int_{\ell a}^{\ell b}\sqrt{2m(E_\star W(x/\ell)-E_\star\lambda)}\,dx =\int_a^b\sqrt{2mE_\star\bigl(W(\xi)-\lambda\bigr)}\,\ell\,d\xi =\sqrt{2mE_\star}\,\ell\int_a^b\sqrt{W(\xi)-\lambda}\,d\xi .$$ Dividing by $\hbar$ and using $\frac{\sqrt{2mE_\star}\,\ell}{\hbar}=\frac1h$ from the definition of $h$ gives (b).

boundaries.reason: The lemma concerns a nonempty open interval I and a physical interval [a,b] with a<b; no empty-set case is asserted.
The scales are strictly positive and the lemma contains no special value at zero of any parameter.
No unit parameter is distinguished; the identities hold for every admissible scale and every lambda.
The only degenerate configurations excluded are W-lambda=0 on [a,b] in clause (b), which is stated as a hypothesis rather than claimed; no degenerate case is left to check.

boundaries.evidence: Step 3.1 integrates the continuous integrand over the compact interval [a,b] with the strict positivity hypothesis, so the endpoint values are included and no endpoint is excluded.

boundaries.reason: The lemma uses only the chain rule and one-dimensional change of variables for continuous integrands; no choice principle is invoked.

boundaries.evidence: Step 2.1 proves the forward implication of the equivalence in (a).
Step 2.2 proves the converse implication of the equivalence in (a).

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on the nonzero
complex Hilbert space $H$. Then there is a unique regular projection valued
measure $E$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ such that
$$
D(T)=\Bigl\{x\in H:\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_x(\lambda)<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad Tx=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE(\lambda)x\quad(x\in D(T)).
$$
Conversely, if $E$ is a regular projection valued measure on $\mathbb R$, then
the operator $\int\lambda\,dE$ with that domain is self-adjoint and its
spectral projection valued measure is $E$ again.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(X,\Sigma)$ be a measurable space
([[def-measurable-space]], [[def-sigma-algebra]]) and let $H$ be a complex
Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). A **projection valued measure** (PVM) on
$(X,\Sigma)$ is a map

$$E:\Sigma\longrightarrow\mathcal B(H),\qquad B\longmapsto E(B),$$

such that:

1. $E(B)$ is an **orthogonal projection** for every $B\in\Sigma$, that is, a
   bounded operator with $E(B)^2=E(B)=E(B)^*$; there is no finite-dimensional
   restriction;
2. $E(\varnothing)=0$ and $E(X)=I$;
3. $E(B\cap C)=E(B)E(C)$ for all $B,C\in\Sigma$;
4. for every pairwise disjoint sequence $(B_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ in $\Sigma$ with
   union $B$ and every $x\in H$, the series $\sum_nE(B_n)x$ converges in norm
   to $E(B)x$, that is
   $$E(B)x=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}E(B_n)x .$$

Clause 4 is **strong countable additivity**. A PVM is called **regular** when
$X$ is a locally compact Hausdorff space ([[def-locally-compact-space]]), the
$\sigma$-algebra is the Borel $\sigma$-algebra, and every one of the finite
positive measures

$$E_x(B):=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle,\qquad x\in H,\ B\in\Sigma,$$

is a regular Borel measure ([[def-regular-borel-measure-on-an-lch-space]]). Inner
products are linear in the first variable and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]); this fixed convention is the one
used for every pairing $E_{x,y}(B)=\langle E(B)x,y\rangle$ on this page.

**Well-definedness: the projection clause.** The conditions $P^2=P=P^*$ are
simultaneously meaningful and describe exactly the Hilbert orthogonal
projections, with no hidden finite-dimensional hypothesis. Indeed, for a
bounded $P$ with $P^2=P=P^*$ the range $\operatorname{ran}P$ is a linear
subspace, and for $y=Pw$ one has
$\langle x-Px,y\rangle=\langle P(x-Px),w\rangle=\langle Px-P^2x,w\rangle=0$, so
$x-Px\perp\operatorname{ran}P$; conversely $\langle Pz,Pz\rangle=\langle z,P^*Pz\rangle=\langle z,Pz\rangle=0$
for $z\perp\operatorname{ran}P$, so $z\in\ker P$, while
$\langle z,Px\rangle=\langle Pz,x\rangle=0$ for $z\in\ker P$ gives
$\ker P=(\operatorname{ran}P)^\perp$
([[thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Hence
$\operatorname{ran}P=(\ker P)^\perp$ is closed, and the two defining properties
$Px\in\operatorname{ran}P$, $x-Px\in(\operatorname{ran}P)^\perp$ of
[[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]] show that $P=P_{\operatorname{ran}P}$ is
the Hilbert orthogonal projection onto a closed subspace, and conversely every
such $P_M$ is idempotent and self-adjoint by
[[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]] and
[[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]]. Finally $P$ is
contractive: from $\langle Px,x\rangle=\langle Px,Px\rangle=\|Px\|^2$ and
Cauchy–Schwarz, $\|Px\|^2\le\|Px\|\,\|x\|$, so $\|Px\|\le\|x\|$ for all $x$,
and $\langle Px,x\rangle=\|Px\|^2\ge0$ is a nonnegative real number.

**Well-definedness: the regularity clause.** For an orthogonal projection value
the pairing $E_x(B)=\langle E(B)x,x\rangle$ is a nonnegative real number and
$E_x(X)=\langle x,x\rangle=\|x\|^2<+\infty$, so every $E_x$ is a finite
nonnegative set function and the regularity requirement is a meaningful
condition on it; that each $E_x$ is genuinely a countably additive measure of
total mass $\|x\|^2$, and that the polarized pairings $E_{x,y}$ are finite
complex measures, is proved as
[[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]] before either is used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on a complex Hilbert space $H$ with
spectral projection valued measure $E$ on $\mathbb R$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]). The **discrete
spectrum** $\sigma_{\mathrm d}(A)$ is the set of eigenvalues of $A$ that are
isolated points of $\sigma(A)$ and whose eigenspace is finite dimensional; the
**essential spectrum** is
$$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A):=\sigma(A)\setminus\sigma_{\mathrm d}(A),$$
with $\sigma(A)$ as in [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]].

For $H=\{0\}$ use its unique PVM directly: the spectrum and both parts
are empty and every projection has rank zero. Below suppose $H\ne\{0\}$,
as required by the cited spectral theorem.

**Spectral-projection description, with proofs.** Fix $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ and write
$P_\varepsilon:=E((\lambda-\varepsilon,\lambda+\varepsilon))$ for
$\varepsilon>0$.

Here rank means the algebraic dimension of the range when finite; rank
$=\infty$ means the range is not finite dimensional. The calculus
[[thm-unbounded-borel-functional-calculus]] gives the support facts:
$E(\mathbb R\setminus\sigma(A))=0$, and every open interval about a
spectral point has nonzero projection. Projections on disjoint sets have
orthogonal ranges, and $E(B)E(C)=E(B\cap C)$
[[def-projection-valued-measure]].

1. *$E(\{\lambda\})$ is the projection onto $\ker(A-\lambda)$.* If
   $x=E(\{\lambda\})x$, its scalar measure $E_x$ is supported on
   $\{\lambda\}$ by the projection identity. Thus
   $\int\mu^2dE_x=\lambda^2\|x\|^2<\infty$, so $x\in D(A)$, and
   $$\|(A-\lambda)x\|^2=\int|\mu-\lambda|^2dE_x=0.$$
   The domain and norm identities are supplied by the unbounded calculus and
   [[lem-unbounded-pvm-integral-is-well-defined-and-closed]]. Hence $Ax=\lambda x$.
   Conversely, for an eigenvector (or the zero vector) the same norm identity
   gives zero integral. On $\{|\mu-\lambda|\ge1/n\}$ this bounds the measure
   by $n^2$ times that zero integral; taking the countable union shows
   $E_x(\mathbb R\setminus\{\lambda\})=0$.
   Since $\|(I-E(\{\lambda\}))x\|^2$ equals this scalar measure,
   $E(\{\lambda\})x=x$.
2. *A finite-rank interval contains only finitely many spectral points.*
   If $P_\varepsilon$ has rank $r<\infty$ and its interval contained $r+1$
   distinct spectral points, choose disjoint small open intervals about those
   finitely many points, all contained in the given interval. Each has a
   nonzero projection by support. Choose one unit vector in each range.
   They are orthonormal vectors in $\operatorname{ran}P_\varepsilon$, hence
   linearly independent (take inner products with each vector), contradicting
   its dimension $r$. Thus there are at most $r$ spectral points there.
   In particular any $\lambda\in\sigma(A)$ with such a finite-rank
   $P_\varepsilon$ is isolated: take a smaller interval around $\lambda$
   excluding the other finitely many points. For that interval the projection
   is $E(\{\lambda\})$ by support, is nonzero by support, and has finite rank
   since its range lies in $\operatorname{ran}P_\varepsilon$. By item 1,
   $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of finite multiplicity.
3. *The two rank characterizations.* If $\lambda\in\sigma_{\mathrm d}(A)$,
   an isolating interval has projection $E(\{\lambda\})$, of finite rank
   by item 1. Conversely, if $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue and some
   $P_\varepsilon$ has finite rank, item 2 proves it discrete. Hence
   $$\lambda\in\sigma_{\mathrm d}(A)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\lambda\text{ is an eigenvalue and some }P_\varepsilon\text{ has finite rank}.$$
   If $\lambda\in\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)$, item 2 excludes every finite-rank
   interval. Conversely, if every $P_\varepsilon$ has infinite rank, each is
   nonzero, so support puts $\lambda$ in $\sigma(A)$, and the just-proved
   discrete characterization excludes it from $\sigma_{\mathrm d}(A)$.
   Therefore
   $$\lambda\in\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{rank}P_\varepsilon=\infty\text{ for every }\varepsilon>0.$$
4. *$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)$ is closed.* If $\lambda_n\in
   \sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)$ and $\lambda_n\to\lambda$, then for every
   $\varepsilon>0$ some $n$ has $(\lambda_n-\varepsilon/2, \lambda_n+
   \varepsilon/2)\subseteq(\lambda-\varepsilon,\lambda+\varepsilon)$, so
   $\operatorname{rank}P_\varepsilon\ge\operatorname{rank}P_{\varepsilon/2}^{(n)}
   =\infty$ and $\lambda\in\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)$ by item 3.

The closure conclusion is in $\mathbb R$, and also in $\mathbb C$ since
$\mathbb R$ is closed there. A spectral accumulation point has infinitely
many spectral points in every surrounding interval, so item 2 forces infinite
rank. An isolated eigenvalue of infinite multiplicity has its infinite-dimensional
eigenspace inside every interval range by item 1. Consequently an accumulation point of $\sigma(A)$ and an isolated eigenvalue of
infinite multiplicity both lie in $\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)$, and $\sigma(A)$
is the disjoint union of $\sigma_{\mathrm d}(A)$ and
$\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(A)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $A$ be self-adjoint on a complex Hilbert space H, with $A\ge cI$ meaning $\langle Ax,x\rangle\ge c\|x\|^2$ for every $x\in D(A)$, for some
real $c$. Put
$$Q(A):=D\bigl((A-cI)^{1/2}\bigr),\qquad q_A[x]:=c\|x\|^2+\bigl\|(A-cI)^{1/2}x\bigr\|^2\quad(x\in Q(A)).$$
Then $Q(A)$ and $q_A$ do not depend on the choice of the constant
$c\le\inf\sigma(A)$ (the form $q_A[x]=\int\lambda\,dE_x$ is itself unchanged,
while the summand $\|(A-cI)^{1/2}x\|^2$ changes by the constant
$(c-c')\|x\|^2$ when $c$ is replaced by $c'\le c$),
$q_A[x]=\int\lambda\,dE_x(\lambda)=\langle Ax,x\rangle$ for $x\in D(A)$, the
domain $D(A)$ is dense in $Q(A)$ for the norm
$\|x\|_Q=(\|x\|^2+\|(A-cI)^{1/2}x\|^2)^{1/2}$, and $q_A$ is a closed quadratic
form with $q_A[x]\ge c\|x\|^2$.

Here the square root is the Borel calculus of $\sqrt{\max(\lambda-c,0)}$; the proof shows that E is carried on $[c,\infty)$. A closed semibounded quadratic form means the diagonal of a Hermitian sesquilinear form on a dense linear domain, complete in the displayed shifted form norm. If H={0}, use the unique PVM and operator and the convention inf(empty spectrum)=+infinity.

[[def-projection-valued-measure]]), put $P:=E(\{E_0\})$, and assume that

$$\sigma(H)\cap(E_0,E_0+g)=\varnothing .$$
For $u\in D(|H|^{1/2})$ write $E_u(B):=\langle E(B)u,u\rangle$ for Borel sets

(a) $q_H[u]-E_0=\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb R}(\lambda-E_0)\,dE_u(\lambda)\ \ge\ g\,\|(I-P)u\|^2$;

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let A be a self-adjoint operator on a complex Hilbert space H, bounded below by c, with form domain Q(A) and form q_A of [[lem-spectral-form-domain-and-core-of-a-semibounded-operator]]. Put $\Lambda=\inf\sigma_{\rm ess}(A)$, with inf(empty)=+infinity. List the eigenvalues below Lambda in nondecreasing order with multiplicity as E_1,E_2,..., setting E_n=Lambda after the list is exhausted. Then for every integer n>=1,
$$E_n=\inf_{\substack{L\subseteq Q(A)\text{ linear}\\\dim L=n}}\ \sup_{\substack{x\in L\\\|x\|=1}}q_A[x]=\sup_{\substack{F\subseteq Q(A)\text{ linear}\\\dim F\le n-1}}\ \inf_{\substack{x\in Q(A)\cap F^\perp\\\|x\|=1}}q_A[x].$$

The second outer family is always nonempty, since it contains {0}. Whenever Q(A) contains an (n-1)-dimensional subspace, the same value is obtained by requiring dim F=n-1. The at-most convention includes the exhausted finite-dimensional case for all n without taking a supremum over an empty outer family.

The first infimum is unchanged if its trial spaces L are restricted to D(A). If E_n<Lambda, both outer values are attained, respectively by spans of the first n and the first n-1 orthonormal eigenvectors (the latter span is {0} when n=1).

$A$-bound less than one ([[def-relative-boundedness-with-respect-to-an-operator]]).
Then $A+B$ with domain $D(A)$ is self-adjoint. If $A$ is merely essentially
self-adjoint and $B$ is symmetric with $D(A)\subseteq D(B)$ and $A$-bound less
than one, then $A+B$ on $D(A)$ is essentially self-adjoint and its closure is
the self-adjoint operator obtained by applying the first part to $\overline A$
and the graph-norm extension of $B|_{D(A)}$ to $D(\overline A)$. If $A\ge\gamma$ and
$(a,b)$ is an admissible pair for $B$ with $a<1$, then
$A+B\ge\gamma-\max\{a|\gamma|+b,\ b/(1-a)\}$.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be an arbitrary complex Hilbert space, let $H_0$ be self-adjoint on its exact dense domain, and use the resolvent convention $R_0(z)=(z-H_0)^{-1}$. Let $E\in\mathbb R$ be an isolated eigenvalue with $\operatorname{dist}(E,\sigma(H_0)\setminus\{E\})\ge g>0$, and suppose its orthogonal spectral projection $P_0=E_{H_0}(\{E\})$ has rank one. Let $V\in\mathcal B(H)$ be self-adjoint with $v=\|V\|>0$, put $H_\lambda=H_0+\lambda V$ on $D(H_0)$, and let $\lambda\in\mathbb C$ satisfy $q=2|\lambda|v/g<1$. Write $\Gamma$ for the counterclockwise circle $|z-E|=g/2$. Then:

(a) $H_\lambda$ is closed and densely defined. For every $z\in\Gamma$, $z-H_\lambda$ is a bijection from $D(H_0)$ onto $H$, with
$$R_\lambda(z)=(z-H_\lambda)^{-1}=R_0(z)\sum_{k\ge0}(\lambda VR_0(z))^k,\qquad \|R_\lambda(z)\|\le\frac{2/g}{1-q},\qquad \|R_\lambda(z)-R_0(z)\|\le\frac{2}{g}\frac{q}{1-q}.$$
The series converges in operator norm uniformly on $\Gamma$ and locally uniformly in the complex disk $|\lambda|<g/(2v)$.

(b) The operator
$$P_\lambda=\frac1{2\pi i}\oint_\Gamma R_\lambda(z)dz$$
is an operator-norm holomorphic, rank-one Riesz projection throughout that disk. Its range lies in $D(H_0)$ and is invariant under $H_\lambda$, and it commutes with $H_\lambda$ on $D(H_0)$. There is exactly one spectral value $E_\lambda$ inside $\Gamma$; it is an eigenvalue of algebraic multiplicity one, with $\operatorname{ran}P_\lambda=\ker(H_\lambda-E_\lambda)$. The function $\lambda\mapsto E_\lambda$ is holomorphic.

(c) $\|P_\lambda-P_0\|\le q/(1-q)$. Rank one holds for every $q<1$, including when this bound is at least one. Whenever two projections $P_\lambda,P_\mu$ have distance less than one, the restrictions $P_\mu|_{\operatorname{ran}P_\lambda}$ and $P_\lambda|_{\operatorname{ran}P_\mu}$ are injective; local comparisons along the path $t\lambda$, $0\le t\le1$, preserve the rank throughout the full disk.

(d) For real $\lambda$, $H_\lambda$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_0)$, $E_\lambda$ is real, and $P_\lambda=E_{H_\lambda}(\{E_\lambda\})$ is its orthogonal spectral projection. For complex $\lambda$, $P_\lambda$ is the Riesz projection; self-adjointness or orthogonality is not asserted.

No separability or Axiom of Choice assumption on $H$ is added. Degenerate clusters are outside this rank-one statement.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and adopt the
hypotheses of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-contour-perturbation-projection]]:
$H_0$ self-adjoint with isolated simple eigenvalue $E$, gap $g>0$, normalized
eigenvector $\psi_0$ with $P_0\psi_0=\psi_0$, $V=V^*\in\mathcal B(H)$ with
$v=\|V\|$, and $q=2|\lambda|v/g<1/2$. Write
$Q=I-P_0$, $H_Q=H_0|_{D(H_0)\cap QH}$ on the reducing space $QH$, and define the reduced inverse
$$S=\iota_Q(H_Q-E)^{-1}Q:H\longrightarrow D(H_0)\cap QH,$$
where $\iota_Q:QH\hookrightarrow H$ is the inclusion (and the zero complementary space gives the zero map). Then $S$ is bounded with $\|S\|\le1/g$; no inverse of $H_0-E$ on all of $H$ is asserted. Let $P_\lambda$, $E_\lambda$ be the perturbed projection and
its unique eigenvalue inside the contour, as in
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-contour-perturbation-projection]]. Define the
gauge-normalized eigenvector
$$\psi(\lambda):=\frac{P_\lambda\psi_0}{\langle P_\lambda\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle}.$$
Then $\psi(\lambda)$ is analytic in $\lambda$ with $\|\psi(\lambda)\|\le3$ for
$q<1/2$, $\langle\psi(\lambda),\psi_0\rangle=1$, and $(H_0+\lambda V)\psi(\lambda)=E_\lambda\psi(\lambda)$.
Moreover the first and second coefficients are
$$E'(0)=\langle V\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle,\qquad \psi'(0)=-SV\psi_0,\qquad E''(0)=-2\langle VSV\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle,$$
where all pairings are finite and the second derivative involves the whole
complementary spectral subspace, not only bound states. Equivalently
$E_\lambda=E+\lambda\langle V\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle-\lambda^2\langle VSV\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle+O(\lambda^3)$
for $|\lambda|$ in the disk of the remainder estimate; the $O(\lambda^3)$ is made
explicit in [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-analytic-perturbation-remainder]].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and the hypotheses of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-simple-level-reduced-resolvent-coefficients]] on an arbitrary complex Hilbert space $H$, with inner product linear in the first variable: $H_0$ is self-adjoint on its exact dense domain, $E$ is an isolated simple eigenvalue with gap at least $g>0$, $\psi_0$ is a normalized eigenvector, and $V=V^*$ is bounded with $v=\|V\|$. Let $P_\lambda,E_\lambda$ be the contour projection and eigenvalue, $Q=I-P_0$, $S=\iota_Q(H_0|_{D(H_0)\cap QH}-E)^{-1}Q$ the actual reduced inverse, and $\psi(\lambda)$ the gauge-fixed eigenvector with $\langle\psi(\lambda),\psi_0\rangle=1$.

For $v>0$ put $R=g/(8v)$. On the full complex disk $|\lambda|<R$:

(a) $q=2|\lambda|v/g\le1/4$, $\|P_\lambda-P_0\|\le1/3$, $\|\psi(\lambda)\|\le2$, and the holomorphic scalar energy identity is
$$E_\lambda=\langle(H_0+\lambda V)\psi(\lambda),\psi_0\rangle=E+\lambda\langle V\psi(\lambda),\psi_0\rangle.$$

(b) The exact coefficients are
$$E'(0)=\langle V\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle,\qquad \psi'(0)=-SV\psi_0,\qquad E''(0)=-2\langle VSV\psi_0,\psi_0\rangle,$$
with bounds $|E'(0)|\le v$, $\|\psi'(0)\|\le v/g$ and $|E''(0)|\le2v^2/g$. The whole complementary spectral subspace, including its continuum, contributes through $S$. The cubic remainder satisfies
$$\left|E_\lambda-E-\lambda E'(0)-\frac{\lambda^2}{2}E''(0)\right|\le\frac{Rv\,(|\lambda|/R)^3}{1-|\lambda|/R}.$$
At $|\lambda|=R/2$ the displayed bound is $Rv/4=g/32$. For $|\lambda|\le R/2$ it is at most $128v^3|\lambda|^3/g^2$.

(c) If $v=0$, then $V=0$ and $P_\lambda=P_0$, $E_\lambda=E$, $\psi(\lambda)=\psi_0$ for every complex $\lambda$; no radius involving division by $v$ is used in this branch.

These conclusions are conditional on the strict positive gap and bounded perturbation, and do not assert an unbounded or degenerate perturbation theorem.

([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],

suppliers.

fix a self-adjoint operator $H_{0}:D(H_{0})\subseteq\mathfrak H\to\mathfrak H$
on the declared state space, **declare** $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$ to be the
unperturbed sharp energy observable,
fix a bounded self-adjoint operator $V\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]) with
$$v:=\|V\|<\infty$$
([[def-operator-norm]]) and fix a real **coupling** $\lambda$ (dimensionless:

$$H(\lambda):=H_{0}+\lambda V,\qquad D(H(\lambda)):=D(H_{0}),$$

([[thm-kato-rellich]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).

reading of the family as the system's energy is the model assumption.

**(c) The gapped label.** Fix an isolated eigenvalue $E\in\mathbb R$ of $H_{0}$
of finite multiplicity $r\ge1$ with gap
$$\operatorname{dist}\bigl(E,\sigma(H_{0})\setminus\{E\}\bigr)\ge g>0,$$
and put $P_{0}:=E_{H_{0}}(\{E\})$ and $Q_{0}:=I-P_{0}$
([[def-discrete-and-essential-spectrum-of-a-self-adjoint-operator]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]],
[[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]]). The
definitions used by the pair are those of the cited suppliers:

(i) for real $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|v<g$, the **followed perturbed label**
$E_{\lambda}$ is the spectral value of $H(\lambda)$ inside the counterclockwise
circle $|z-E|=g/2$, and $P_{\lambda}$ is its Riesz projection of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-contour-perturbation-projection]] clause (b); for
such $\lambda$ the label is unique and $P_{\lambda}$ is the orthogonal spectral
projection of $H(\lambda)$ at $E_{\lambda}$; at $\lambda=0$ one has
$E_{0}=E$ and $P_{0}$ as displayed;

(ii) the **first-order operator** is the Hermitian operator
$$V_{E}:=\bigl(P_{0}VP_{0}\bigr)\big|_{P_{0}\mathfrak H}$$
on the finite-dimensional eigenspace $P_{0}\mathfrak H$, whose spectrum
$\operatorname{spec}(V_{E})\subseteq[-v,v]$ is the model's first-order shift
data (joules per unit coupling);

(iii) the **complementary reduced inverse**
$$S:=\iota_{Q_{0}}\bigl(H_{0}|_{D(H_{0})\cap Q_{0}\mathfrak H}-E\bigr)^{-1}Q_{0}$$
is the bounded operator of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-simple-level-reduced-resolvent-coefficients]]
when $r=1$, and the analogous bounded reduced inverse $B(z)$ of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-degenerate-feshbach-error]] clause (a) for
general $r$; its role is to record that the **whole** complementary spectral
subspace, continuum included, contributes to the second-order data.

**(d) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) cover bounded perturbations of a self-adjoint
operator and a fixed isolated finite-multiplicity label only. The definition
asserts no time-dependent perturbation, no adiabatic ramping of $\lambda$, no
statement that a preparation occupies the branch of $E_{\lambda}$ or of any
eigenvalue of $V_{E}$, no branch-population or relaxation statement, no
measurement and no identification of the model with a laboratory system; the

$x\in[a,b]$, let $h>0$, put $\theta(x):=\int_a^xp(s)\,ds$ and
$$w_\pm(x):=p(x)^{-1/2}e^{\pm i\theta(x)/h},\qquad q(x):=\frac{3p'(x)^2}{4p(x)^2}-\frac{p''(x)}{2p(x)}.$$
Then:

(a) $w_\pm\in C^2([a,b])$ and $w_\pm''+\dfrac{p^2}{h^2}w_\pm=q\,w_\pm$ pointwise on
$[a,b]$.

(b) The Wronskian $W:=w_+w_-'-w_+'w_-$ equals $-2i/h$ on $[a,b]$.

(c) Let $y\in C^2([a,b])$ solve $y''+\dfrac{p^2}{h^2}y=0$, let
$M(x):=\begin{pmatrix}w_+(x)&w_-(x)\\ w_+'(x)&w_-'(x)\end{pmatrix}$ and
$c(x):=\bigl(c_+(x),c_-(x)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}:=M(x)^{-1}\bigl(y(x),y'(x)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}$
(well defined by (b)). Then $c\in C^1([a,b];\mathbb C^2)$ and $c'=B(x)c$ with
$$B(x)=\frac{q(x)}{W}\begin{pmatrix}w_+(x)w_-(x)&w_-(x)^2\\ -w_+(x)^2&-w_+(x)w_-(x)\end{pmatrix},$$
and with $\|\cdot\|_1$ the $\ell^1$ norm on $\mathbb C^2$ one has
$\|B(x)\|_1=\dfrac{h|q(x)|}{p(x)}$ for every $x\in[a,b]$.

In particular $y=w_+c_++w_-c_-$, and the coefficient system is a nonsingular
linear ODE with explicitly bounded coefficients. No approximation of $y$ and no
physical interpretation is asserted here.

$$\zeta(x):=\operatorname{sign}(x)\Bigl[\frac32\Bigl|\int_0^x\sqrt{|q(s)|}\,ds\Bigr|\Bigr]^{2/3},\qquad a(x):=(\zeta'(x))^{-1/2},\qquad u(x)=a(x)w(\zeta(x)).$$
Then:

(a) $\zeta\in C^4$, $\zeta(\zeta')^2=q$, $\zeta'>0$ with
$\min\zeta'>0$, and $a>0$ is $C^3$;

(b) $w$ satisfies $w''(\zeta)=\bigl[\zeta/h^2+R(\zeta)\bigr]w(\zeta)$ with
$$R(\zeta)=-\frac{a''(\zeta)}{a(\zeta)\,(\zeta')^2},$$
a continuous bounded real function on $\zeta([-x_-,x_+])$;

(c) the constants implicit in (a)–(b) depend only on $q$ and the interval.

Then:

(a) the integral converges absolutely on compact sets and $A$ is entire with
$A''(z)=zA(z)$;

(b) for real $z$, after deforming each ray to the imaginary axis,
$$A(z)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{i(t^3/3+zt)}\,dt$$

$$T(h)=e^{-2S}\bigl[1+O\bigl(\varepsilon(h)+e^{-2S}\bigr)\bigr],$$
quantitatively
$$|T(h)e^{2S}-1|\le\frac{C_0[\varepsilon(h)+e^{-2S}]}{1-C_0[\varepsilon(h)+e^{-2S}]}$$
whenever the denominator is positive. The bound holds for fixed $V,E$ with the
stated separated simple turning points; rectangular walls, coalescing turning
points, barrier-top uniformity and resonant multiwell interference are excluded.

Let $q\in C^5([-x_-,x_+])$ be real, with a single simple zero at $0$:
$q(0)=0$, $q'(0)>0$, $q(x)$ has the sign of $x$, and $q\ne0$ on
$[-x_-,0)\cup(0,x_+]$. Let $h>0$ and consider $u''=q(x)u/h^2$ on the interval.
Define
$$\zeta(x):=\operatorname{sign}(x)\Bigl[\frac32\Bigl|\int_0^x\sqrt{|q(s)|}\,ds\Bigr|\Bigr]^{2/3},\qquad a(x):=(\zeta'(x))^{-1/2},\qquad u(x)=a(x)w(\zeta(x)).$$
Then:

(a) $\zeta\in C^4$, $\zeta(\zeta')^2=q$, $\zeta'>0$ with
$\min\zeta'>0$, and $a>0$ is $C^3$;

(b) $w$ satisfies $w''(\zeta)=\bigl[\zeta/h^2+R(\zeta)\bigr]w(\zeta)$ with
$$R(\zeta)=-\frac{a''(\zeta)}{a(\zeta)\,(\zeta')^2},$$
a continuous bounded real function on $\zeta([-x_-,x_+])$;

(c) the constants implicit in (a)–(b) depend only on $q$ and the interval.

Adopt the hypotheses and notation of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-liouville-turning-point-transformation]]: $q\in C^5$
with a single simple zero at $0$, $q'(0)>0$, transformed equation
$w''=[\zeta/h^2+R(\zeta)]w$ on $\zeta([-x_-,x_+])$, $a>0$ the Liouville factor
and $R$ continuous bounded. Let
$A_h(\zeta):=A(\zeta/h^{2/3})$, $B_h(\zeta):=B(\zeta/h^{2/3})$ for the Airy
functions of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-airy-envelopes-and-asymptotic-coefficients]]
(Wronskian $A_hB_h'-A_h'B_h=h^{-2/3}/\pi$), and define the envelopes
$$e_h(\zeta):=\bigl(1+|\zeta|/h^{2/3}\bigr)^{-1/4}\exp\Bigl(-\frac{2(\zeta_+)^{3/2}}{3h}\Bigr),\qquad d_h(\zeta):=h^{-2/3}\bigl(1+|\zeta|/h^{2/3}\bigr)^{1/4}\exp\Bigl(-\frac{2(\zeta_+)^{3/2}}{3h}\Bigr).$$
Then:

(a) *Volterra representation.* For $h$ small the unique solution with Airy terminal data $w(c)=A_h(c)$, $w'(c)=A_h'(c)$ at the right endpoint $\zeta=c$ satisfies
$$w(\zeta)=A_h(\zeta)+\pi h^{2/3}\int_\zeta^c\bigl[A_h(\zeta)B_h(v)-B_h(\zeta)A_h(v)\bigr]R(v)w(v)\,dv .$$

(b) *Stable weighted estimate.* There is a constant $C_A$ with
$|w(\zeta)-A_h(\zeta)|\le C_Ae_h(\zeta)(e^{\varepsilon_h}-1)$ and
$|w'(\zeta)-A_h'(\zeta)|\le C_Ad_h(\zeta)(e^{\varepsilon_h}-1)$, where
$$\varepsilon_h:=Ch\int_{-b}^c\frac{|R(v)|}{\sqrt{|v|+h^{2/3}}}\,dv\le C'h$$
for constants depending only on $q$ and the interval.

(c) *Growing branch and connection.* The solution with terminal data
$(B_h,B_h')$ at $\zeta=0$ obeys the analogous bound with $e_h$ replaced by its
growing analogue on the full interval; consequently, for fixed $\zeta>0$ and
$\zeta<0$ away from zero, the forbidden-side solution
$q^{-1/4}\exp(-\frac1h\int_0^x\sqrt q)$ corresponds to
$2(-q)^{-1/4}\sin(\frac1h\int_x^0\sqrt{-q}+\pi/4)$ on the allowed side, and the
growing forbidden solution to the corresponding cosine, with absolute errors bounded by the envelopes times $C(\varepsilon_h+h/|\zeta|^{3/2})$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $A$ be the
entire Airy function of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-airy-contour-and-fresnel-normalization]] and
define, for real $z$,
$$B(z):=\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty\Bigl[\exp\bigl(-t^3/3+zt\bigr)+\sin\bigl(t^3/3+zt\bigr)\Bigr]dt .$$
Then:

(a) $B$ is well defined and smooth on $\mathbb R$, extends to an entire
solution of $B''=zB$, and the Wronskian identity
$$A(z)B'(z)-A'(z)B(z)=\frac1\pi$$
holds for all complex $z$;

(b) as $Z\to+\infty$, with $\Theta=2Z^{3/2}/3+\pi/4$,
$$B(Z)=\frac1{\sqrt\pi}Z^{-1/4}e^{2Z^{3/2}/3}\bigl(1+O(Z^{-3/2})\bigr),\quad B'(Z)=\frac1{\sqrt\pi}Z^{1/4}e^{2Z^{3/2}/3}\bigl(1+O(Z^{-3/2})\bigr),$$
$$B(-Z)=\frac1{\sqrt\pi}Z^{-1/4}\bigl(\cos\Theta+O(Z^{-3/2})\bigr),\quad B'(-Z)=\frac1{\sqrt\pi}Z^{1/4}\bigl(\sin\Theta+O(Z^{-3/2})\bigr);$$

(c) *Envelopes.* With $p(z):=1+|z|$ and $S(z):=\frac23(z_+)^{3/2}$ there is a
constant $C<\infty$ with
$$|A(z)|\le Cp(z)^{-1/4}e^{-S(z)},\quad|B(z)|\le Cp(z)^{-1/4}e^{S(z)},\quad |A'(z)|\le Cp(z)^{1/4}e^{-S(z)},\quad|B'(z)|\le Cp(z)^{1/4}e^{S(z)}$$
for all real $z$, and there is $c>0$ with
$A(z)\ge cp(z)^{-1/4}e^{-S(z)}$ for $z\ge0$.

Adopt the hypotheses and notation of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-allowed-region-wkb-coefficient-equation]]: $p\in
C^2([a,b])$ positive, $h>0$, $\theta(x)=\int_a^xp$, $w_\pm=p^{-1/2}e^{\pm
i\theta/h}$, $q=\frac{3p'^2}{4p^2}-\frac{p''}{2p}$, $M$ the fundamental matrix
of $(w_+,w_-)$ and $c=M^{-1}(y,y')^{\mathsf T}$ the coefficient curve of an exact
solution $y\in C^2([a,b])$ of $y''+\frac{p^2}{h^2}y=0$. Then for every
$x\in[a,b]$:

(a) *Growth bound.* $\|c(x)\|_1\le\|c(a)\|_1\exp\Bigl(h\displaystyle\int_a^x
\frac{|q(s)|}{p(s)}\,ds\Bigr)$.

(b) *Deviation bound.*
$$\|c(x)-c(a)\|_1\le\|c(a)\|_1\Bigl(\exp\Bigl(h\int_a^x\frac{|q(s)|}{p(s)}\,ds\Bigr)-1\Bigr).$$

(c) *Pointwise wavefunction error.* With $\Psi(x):=c_+(a)w_+(x)+c_-(a)w_-(x)$
the leading WKB wave,
$$|y(x)-\Psi(x)|\le p(x)^{-1/2}\|c(a)\|_1\Bigl(\exp\Bigl(h\int_a^x\frac{|q(s)|}{p(s)}\,ds\Bigr)-1\Bigr).$$

The estimate degenerates as $p\to0$ (turning points are excluded by the
hypotheses) and asserts nothing about connecting asymptotics across a turning
point; it is an explicit finite-interval error bound of Gronwall type.

**(a) Framework data and line model.** Adopt P1, P2, P4 and P5
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), the
state and observable readings cited there, and the declared effective
one-dimensional line model
[[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]] with a mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s=0$, action constant $\hbar>0$ and units from
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a real potential
$$V\in C_c^{5}(\mathbb R;\mathbb R)$$
(five times continuously differentiable with compact support); it is real,
bounded and measurable, so the line model's assigned energy operator $H_{V}$
of its clause (c) is defined with domain $D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb
C)$, acts by $H_{V}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}D^{2}f+Vf$, and its stationary
equation at energy $E$ reads
$$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\,\psi''+V\psi=E\psi$$
for classically $C^{2}$ solutions.

**(b) Reference scales and nondimensionalisation.** As an additional model
assumption of the pair fix a **reference length** $\ell>0$ (metres) and a
**reference energy** $E_\star>0$ (joules), and put
$$W(\xi):=\frac{V(\ell\xi)}{E_\star},\qquad \lambda:=\frac{E}{E_\star},\qquad h:=\frac{\hbar}{\ell\sqrt{2mE_\star}} .$$
Then $W\in C_c^{5}(\mathbb R;\mathbb R)$ is dimensionless with support scaled by
$\ell$, and $h>0$ is dimensionless. By
[[lem-nrqm-approximations-scaled-line-model-correspondence]] the physical
stationary equation of clause (a) at energy $E$ is equivalent, under
$x=\ell\xi$, $\psi(\ell\xi)=u(\xi)$, to the **dimensionless WKB equation**
$$u''(\xi)=\frac{W(\xi)-\lambda}{h^{2}}\,u(\xi),\qquad \xi\in I,$$
on every interval $I$, and the physical WKB phase integral over a subinterval
$[x_{a},x_{b}]=\ell[a,b]$ with $V>E$ (respectively $V<E$) equals $1/h$ times
the corresponding dimensionless integral, as stated in clause (b) of that
lemma. The pair calls $h$ the model's **semiclassical parameter** and calls
$h\ll1$ the **semiclassical regime**; the physical content of the regime is
$\hbar\ll\ell\sqrt{2mE_\star}$, and every statement of the page's theorems is
an exact statement about the family indexed by $h$, with the error bounds
stated at each $h$.

**(c) Turning points, regions and phase.** For the data $(W,\lambda)$ put
$$\tau:=\{\xi\in\mathbb R: W(\xi)=\lambda\}$$
for the set of **turning points**. A point $\xi_{0}\in\tau$ is **simple** when
$W'(\xi_{0})\ne0$. An open interval $J$ is an **allowed interval** when
$W(\xi)-\lambda<0$ on $J$ (the dimensionless kinetic energy $-(W-\lambda)$ is
positive there), a **forbidden interval** when $W(\xi)-\lambda>0$ on
$J$. On an allowed interval the model uses the local wavenumber
$$p(\xi):=\sqrt{\lambda-W(\xi)}>0$$
and the WKB phase $\theta(\xi):=\int_{\xi_{\mathrm{ref}}}^{\xi}p(s)\,ds$ with a
declared base point; on a forbidden interval the model uses
$\kappa(\xi):=\sqrt{\lambda-W(\xi)}>0$. The **WKB exponent** of a forbidden
interval $[\xi_{a},\xi_{b}]$ is
$$S:=\int_{\xi_{a}}^{\xi_{b}}\sqrt{W(\xi)-\lambda}\,d\xi =\frac1\hbar\int_{x_{a}}^{x_{b}}\sqrt{2m(V(x)-E)}\,dx,$$
the equality being the lemma's clause (b) with $\xi_{a,b}=x_{a,b}/\ell$. The
three declared regime hypotheses used by the page are:

(W1) **Allowed-interval regularity**: $W\in C^{2}$ on a neighbourhood of
$[a,b]$ and $\lambda-W\ge\delta>0$ on $[a,b]$ for some $\delta>0$ (no turning
point in the interval; the interval is allowed);

(W2) **Separated simple turning points**: $W-\lambda$ has exactly two zeros
$\xi_{a}<\xi_{b}$ in $\mathbb R$, both simple, is positive on
$(\xi_{a},\xi_{b})$ and negative on the complement of $[\xi_{a},\xi_{b}]$
(equivalently the physical barrier $V-E$ has exactly two simple zeros
surrounding a forbidden region and is negative outside);

(W3) **Single simple turning point**: on an interval $[\xi_{0}-r,\xi_{0}+s]$
the equation $W-\lambda$ has the single zero $\xi_{0}$, it is simple, and
$W-\lambda<0$ on one side and $>0$ on the other.

**(d) Declared barrier transmission reading.** For $\ell$, $E_\star$, $m$,
$\hbar$, $V$, $E$ satisfying (W2), the model declares a **declared scattering
solution** at energy $E$ to be a solution $u$ of the dimensionless equation
which is oscillatory on both outer allowed sides with in-going/out-going WKB
amplitudes fixed by the matching construction of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-two-turn-barrier-tunnelling-error]], and
declares the **transmission coefficient** $T(h)$ to be the modulus-squared
ratio of the out-going to the in-going amplitude in that normalization
(equivalently, in the model's reading, the transmitted fraction of the
reference probability current). This is a declared model quantity of the
matching construction; no detector, wave packet, scattering experiment or
measured count is asserted, and clause (d) does not by itself assert any
formula for $T(h)$.

**(e) Scope.** The model concerns a declared spinless massive particle in the
declared one-dimensional line model with a compactly supported $C^{5}$
potential, at a fixed energy, in the nondimensionalised family of clause (b).
It asserts nothing about two- or three-dimensional scattering, about singular
or non-smooth potentials, about wave packets, detectors or measurements, and
about any laboratory realization of the line model, the potential $V$ or the
energy $E$.

derivations.claim: [Hypothesis matching] Hypothesis (W2) supplies exactly the two simple zeros $\xi_{a}<\xi_{b}$ with $W-\lambda$ positive between and negative outside; since $V\in C_{c}^{5}$ and $E_\star>0$, the function $W=V(\ell\,\cdot)/E_\star$ is in $C_c^{5}$, and $\lambda\in(0,\max W)$ because the barrier has a positive forbidden region; the derivative of $W-\lambda$ does not vanish at $\xi_{a},\xi_{b}$ because the zeros are simple. Under the identification of [F3] the supplier's equation is the model's equation $u''=(W-\lambda)u/h^{2}$ and its forbidden-region action integral is $B=S$.

[Physical exponent] By [[lem-nrqm-approximations-scaled-line-model-correspondence]] clause (b) applied on the forbidden interval $[\xi_{a},\xi_{b}]$, with $a$ the lower and $b$ the upper endpoint there, $$\frac1h\int_{\xi_{a}}^{\xi_{b}}\sqrt{W-\lambda}\,d\xi =\frac1\hbar\int_{x_{a}}^{x_{b}}\sqrt{2m\bigl(E_\star W(x/\ell)-E_\star\lambda\bigr)}\,dx =\frac1\hbar\int_{x_{a}}^{x_{b}}\sqrt{2m(V(x)-E)}\,dx,$$ which is the displayed identity for $S/h$. The sign is positive because $W-\lambda>0$ and $V-E>0$ on the open interval.

[Transfer of the asymptotic error] Applying [F1] under the identification of step 1.1 gives, for the model's declared transmission datum, the quantitative bound $|T(h)e^{2S/h}-1|\le C_{0}[\varepsilon(h)+e^{-2S/h}]/(1-C_{0}[\varepsilon(h) +e^{-2S/h}])$ whenever the denominator is positive, with $\varepsilon(h)\le C_{1}h$ and constants depending only on the barrier data and the matching sections; the vanishing of the right-hand side gives $T(h)=e^{-2S/h}(1+O(\varepsilon(h)+e^{-2S/h}))$ and, taking $h\downarrow0$ along the fixed barrier, $\lim_{h\downarrow0}T(h)e^{2S/h}=1$.

[Scope] The excluded configurations (rectangular walls, coalescing or multiple turning points, barrier-top uniformity, resonances) are exactly the configurations excluded by [F1]; the model's clause (d) supplies $T(h)$ as a declared matching datum, and no wave packet, detector, apparatus or sampling model entered the argument. This proves the scope statement.

Adopt the framework data and the declared perturbed-family model of
[[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-perturbed-family-model]] in the
**simple-label case**: $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$, $V=V^{*}\in
\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ with $v=\|V\|>0$, $H(\lambda)=H_{0}+\lambda V$ on
$D(H_{0})$ for real $\lambda$, and $E$ is an isolated eigenvalue of $H_{0}$ of
**multiplicity one** with gap at least $g>0$,
$\operatorname{dist}(E,\sigma(H_{0})\setminus\{E\})\ge g$. Let $\psi_{0}$ be a
normalized eigenvector, $P_{0}\psi_{0}=\psi_{0}$, let
$$S:=\iota_{Q_{0}}\bigl(H_{0}|_{D(H_{0})\cap Q_{0}\mathfrak H}-E\bigr)^{-1}Q_{0}, \qquad Q_{0}=I-P_{0},$$
be the reduced inverse of the model clause (c)(iii), and put
$$R:=\frac{g}{8v}.$$
Then for every real $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|<R$:

(a) $H(\lambda)$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$; the model's followed label
$E_{\lambda}$ of the contour $|z-E|=g/2$ exists, is the unique spectral value
of $H(\lambda)$ inside that contour, is real, and its spectral projection is
the orthogonal rank-one projection
$P_{\lambda}=E_{H(\lambda)}(\{E_{\lambda}\})$;

(b) the gauge-fixed eigenvector
$$\psi(\lambda):=\frac{P_{\lambda}\psi_{0}}{\langle P_{\lambda}\psi_{0},\psi_{0}\rangle}$$
is analytic in $\lambda$, satisfies $\langle\psi(\lambda),\psi_{0}\rangle=1$
and $(H_{0}+\lambda V)\psi(\lambda)=E_{\lambda}\psi(\lambda)$, and
$$q:=2|\lambda|v/g\le\tfrac14,\qquad \|P_{\lambda}-P_{0}\|\le\tfrac13,\qquad \|\psi(\lambda)\|\le2 ;$$

(c) the model's label identity
$$E_{\lambda}=\bigl\langle (H_{0}+\lambda V)\psi(\lambda),\psi_{0}\bigr\rangle =E+\lambda\langle V\psi(\lambda),\psi_{0}\rangle$$
holds, so the deviation $\lambda\mapsto E_{\lambda}-E$ of the model's energy
label is controlled by the perturbation alone;

(d) the exact coefficients are
$$E'(0)=\langle V\psi_{0},\psi_{0}\rangle,\qquad \psi'(0)=-SV\psi_{0},\qquad E''(0)=-2\langle VSV\psi_{0},\psi_{0}\rangle,$$
with $|E'(0)|\le v$, $\|\psi'(0)\|\le v/g$ and $|E''(0)|\le2v^{2}/g$; the
second-order coefficient involves the whole complementary spectral subspace of
$H_{0}$ through $S$, continuum included;

(e) the cubic remainder obeys
$$\left|E_{\lambda}-E-\lambda E'(0)-\frac{\lambda^{2}}{2}E''(0)\right| \le \frac{Rv\,(|\lambda|/R)^{3}}{1-|\lambda|/R},$$
so at $|\lambda|=R/2$ the bound is $g/32$ and for $|\lambda|\le R/2$ it is at
most $128v^{3}|\lambda|^{3}/g^{2}$;

(f) if $v=0$, that is $V=0$, then $P_{\lambda}=P_{0}$, $E_{\lambda}=E$ and
$\psi(\lambda)=\psi_{0}$ for every real $\lambda$, and no radius involving
division by $v$ is used in this branch;

(g) the theorem is conditional on the strict positive gap, on the multiplicity
one of $E$ and on the boundedness of $V$; it asserts no unbounded or
degenerate perturbation theorem, no time-dependent perturbation, and no
statement about which branch of the family a preparation occupies.

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt P1, P2 and P4
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) for a declared system, with the
state, sharp-observable and evolution readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematical
suppliers.

**(b) The perturbed family.** As an additional model assumption of the pair,
fix a self-adjoint operator $H_{0}:D(H_{0})\subseteq\mathfrak H\to\mathfrak H$
on the declared state space, **declare** $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$ to be the
unperturbed sharp energy observable,
fix a bounded self-adjoint operator $V\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]) with
$$v:=\|V\|<\infty$$
([[def-operator-norm]]) and fix a real **coupling** $\lambda$ (dimensionless:
$\lambda V$ is read in joules). Declare the **perturbed family**
$$H(\lambda):=H_{0}+\lambda V,\qquad D(H(\lambda)):=D(H_{0}),$$
to be the model's sharp energy observable at coupling $\lambda$. Since $V$ is
$H_{0}$-bounded with $H_{0}$-bound $0\le a<1$ (the bound inequality holds with
$a=0$ and $b=v$), the Kato-Rellich theorem applies and $H(\lambda)$ is
self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$ for every real $\lambda$
([[thm-kato-rellich]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).
This self-adjointness is a supplied theorem about the declared operators; the
reading of the family as the system's energy is the model assumption.

**(c) The gapped label.** Fix an isolated eigenvalue $E\in\mathbb R$ of $H_{0}$
of finite multiplicity $r\ge1$ with gap
$$\operatorname{dist}\bigl(E,\sigma(H_{0})\setminus\{E\}\bigr)\ge g>0,$$
and put $P_{0}:=E_{H_{0}}(\{E\})$ and $Q_{0}:=I-P_{0}$
([[def-discrete-and-essential-spectrum-of-a-self-adjoint-operator]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]],
[[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]]). The
definitions used by the pair are those of the cited suppliers:

(i) for real $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|v<g$, the **followed perturbed label**
$E_{\lambda}$ is the spectral value of $H(\lambda)$ inside the counterclockwise
circle $|z-E|=g/2$, and $P_{\lambda}$ is its Riesz projection of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-contour-perturbation-projection]] clause (b); for
such $\lambda$ the label is unique and $P_{\lambda}$ is the orthogonal spectral
projection of $H(\lambda)$ at $E_{\lambda}$; at $\lambda=0$ one has
$E_{0}=E$ and $P_{0}$ as displayed;

(ii) the **first-order operator** is the Hermitian operator
$$V_{E}:=\bigl(P_{0}VP_{0}\bigr)\big|_{P_{0}\mathfrak H}$$
on the finite-dimensional eigenspace $P_{0}\mathfrak H$, whose spectrum
$\operatorname{spec}(V_{E})\subseteq[-v,v]$ is the model's first-order shift
data (joules per unit coupling);

(iii) the **complementary reduced inverse**
$$S:=\iota_{Q_{0}}\bigl(H_{0}|_{D(H_{0})\cap Q_{0}\mathfrak H}-E\bigr)^{-1}Q_{0}$$
is the bounded operator of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-simple-level-reduced-resolvent-coefficients]]
when $r=1$, and the analogous bounded reduced inverse $B(z)$ of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-degenerate-feshbach-error]] clause (a) for
general $r$; its role is to record that the **whole** complementary spectral
subspace, continuum included, contributes to the second-order data.

**(d) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) cover bounded perturbations of a self-adjoint
operator and a fixed isolated finite-multiplicity label only. The definition
asserts no time-dependent perturbation, no adiabatic ramping of $\lambda$, no
statement that a preparation occupies the branch of $E_{\lambda}$ or of any
eigenvalue of $V_{E}$, no branch-population or relaxation statement, no
measurement and no identification of the model with a laboratory system; the
labels $E_{\lambda}$ are spectral data of the declared family.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework, for systems in the declared massive-matter sector, the following statements about states and their composition. Assume throughout the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is the choice hypothesis of the mathematical suppliers cited below.

**(i) State space.** To each physical system of the sector the model assigns a complex Hilbert space $H$ that is nonzero and separable: a complex Hilbert space in the sense of [[def-hilbert-space]] which admits a sequence whose range is dense in $H$, so that the hypothesis of [[thm-separable-hilbert-space-has-a-countable-orthonormal-basis]] holds and $H$ has a finite or countable orthonormal basis. The assignment of a Hilbert space to a physical system is a model assumption; the linear structure used to combine descriptions mathematically is not an empirical claim. The physical system to which $H$ is assigned, and the sector in which the assignment is made, are declared with it.

**(ii) Pure preparations.** A **pure preparation** of the system is a unit ray $[\psi]=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a vector $\psi\in H$ with $\|\psi\|=1$; that is, two nonzero vectors describe the same pure preparation exactly when they differ by a nonzero complex factor. The zero vector is not a state and no preparation is assigned to it: the normalization $\|\psi\|=1$ is part of the assignment. The ray allows arbitrary nonzero rescaling; between unit representatives the factor has modulus one and is a **global phase**, which has no observable consequence (P2). The rank-one operator $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] is the density operator associated with the ray of $\psi$.

**(iii) General preparations and mixing.** A general preparation of the system is a **density operator**: a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ on $H$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)). Pure preparations are the special case $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ with $\|\psi\|=1$. A **statistical mixture** of preparations $\rho_{n}$ with weights $w_{n}\ge0$, $\sum_{n}w_{n}=1$, is the trace-norm convergent sum $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ as follows directly in the trace-class Banach space ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]): each density has trace norm one, so $\sum_n\|w_n\rho_n\|_1=1$ gives trace-norm convergence. Every partial sum is positive; operator-norm convergence preserves its nonnegative quadratic forms, and continuity of trace gives $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). Thus the limit is again a density operator, without requiring the components to be orthogonal pure states. The weights are a classical preparation uncertainty and are not amplitudes. Distinct weighted ensembles of pure states may define the same $\rho$.

**(iv) Composition.** Two independent distinguishable subsystems with state spaces $H_{A}$ and $H_{B}$ are composed by the completed Hilbert tensor product $H_{A}\widehat\otimes H_{B}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. **(v) Restrictions that are separate assumptions.** Restrictions of the state space by superselection rules, identical-particle symmetry sectors, and the replacement of the tensor product by more general algebraic structures are not consequences of the clauses above: where such a restriction is used it is adopted separately, and the identical-species sectors are the subject of the postulate P6 of this page.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model within its declared sector. They are not derived from experiment, and they do not assert that a physical system is exactly described by such a Hilbert space; no numerical measurement is recorded. The compatibility of the framework with observation is a question about fully specified models and reported data, in the sense of P7.

declared one-centre Coulomb model
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clauses (a)-(c) with
parameters $\hbar>0$, $m>0$ and coupling $\kappa>0$, its assigned energy
operator $H_{\kappa}$ with length scale $a_{\kappa}=\hbar^{2}/(m\kappa)$, and
the energy-observable content of
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]]
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For $n\ge1$, $0\le l\le n-1$, $-l\le m\le l$ let
$\psi_{nlm}$ be the regular bound solutions of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-negative-subspace-completeness-and-degeneracy]] and put
$\Psi_{nlm}:=\psi_{nlm}/\|\psi_{nlm}\|$, and put
$$E_{n}:=-\frac{m\kappa^{2}}{2\hbar^{2}n^{2}}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2ma_{\kappa}^{2}n^{2}}\qquad(n\ge1).$$
Then:

(a) for every label, $\Psi_{nlm}\in D(H_{\kappa})$, $\|\Psi_{nlm}\|=1$,
$H_{\kappa}\Psi_{nlm}=E_{n}\Psi_{nlm}$, and vectors with distinct labels are
orthogonal; the vectors $\Psi_{nlm}$ of fixed $n$ span a subspace of dimension
$\sum_{l=0}^{n-1}(2l+1)=n^{2}$;

(b) the eigenvalues of $H_{\kappa}$ are exactly the numbers $E_{n}$, $n\ge1$;
the eigenspace of $H_{\kappa}$ at $E_{n}$ is exactly
$\operatorname{span}\{\Psi_{nlm}:0\le l\le n-1,\ -l\le m\le l\}$, so the model
assigns to the level $n$ the **model degeneracy** $n^{2}$; in particular
$H_{\kappa}$ has no eigenvalues in $[0,+\infty)$, whose spectral content is
entirely essential spectrum $[0,+\infty)$ in the sense of
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]] (a);

(c) the family
$(\Psi_{nlm})_{n\ge1,\,0\le l\le n-1,\,-l\le m\le l}$ is a complete orthonormal
family of the negative spectral subspace
$E_{H_{\kappa}}((-\infty,0))L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$: the bound states
span exactly the preparations whose energy outcomes are negative almost surely;

(d) the family is not complete in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$: the
nonnegative spectral subspace $E_{H_{\kappa}}([0,+\infty))L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
is nonzero, indeed infinite dimensional, and every unit vector $\psi$ in it has
$\mu^{H_{\kappa}}_{\psi}(B)=0$ for every Borel $B\subseteq(-\infty,0)$, i.e.
strictly negative energy outcomes have probability zero in such a preparation;
consequently the bound states of the model do not exhaust its state space and
the model possesses continuum states which are not bound states;

(e) *Energy-law reading.* For every unit vector $\psi$ the restriction of the
energy outcome law to the negative half-line is the discrete law
$\sum_{n\ge1}w_{n}\delta_{E_{n}}$ with weights
$w_{n}:=\|E_{H_{\kappa}}(\{E_{n}\})\psi\|^{2}\ge0$ and
$\sum_{n\ge1}w_{n}=\|E_{H_{\kappa}}((-\infty,0))\psi\|^{2}\le1$; for
$\psi=\Psi_{nlm}$ the whole law is the point mass $\delta_{E_{n}}$;

(f) *Scope.* The statement is conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, the declared
Coulomb model and the cited mathematics. The values $E_{n}$ are model
parameters determined by $\hbar,m,\kappa$; no numerical value, no measured
line, no transition rate, no photon or light-matter coupling and no empirical
result is asserted. The absolute continuity of the positive spectral subspace
is recorded by the cited mathematics for the unscaled operator and is not
restated for the scaled model here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\gamma>0$, let
$C=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ be as above, let
$(\psi_{nlm})$ be the bound eigenfunctions of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-negative-subspace-completeness-and-degeneracy]], and for
$i=1,2,3$ define the coordinate multiplication operator
$$Q_i\psi:=(\xi\mapsto\xi_i\,\psi(\xi)),\qquad D(Q_i):=\{\psi\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C):\xi_i\psi\in L^2\}.$$
Write also $Q_0:=x_3$ and $Q_\pm:=(x_1\pm ix_2)/\sqrt2$. Then:

(a) each $Q_i$ is self-adjoint on $D(Q_i)$, the domain is a proper dense subspace of $L^2$, and every bound state satisfies $\psi_{nlm}\in D(Q_i)$, with $\|Q_i\psi_{nlm}\|_2^2=\int_0^\infty r^2|u_{nl}(r)|^2dr\cdot\int_{S^2}|\Omega_iY_{lm}(\Omega)|^2d\sigma(\Omega)<\infty$;

(b) for all labels and each $q\in\{-1,0,1\}$ the matrix element $\langle\psi_{n'l'm'},Q_q\psi_{nlm}\rangle$ is absolutely convergent and factors as
$$\langle\psi_{n'l'm'},Q_q\psi_{nlm}\rangle=\Bigl(\int_0^\infty r\,u_{n'l'}(r)\overline{u_{nl}(r)}\,dr\Bigr)\Bigl(\int_{S^2}Y_{l'm'}(\Omega)\overline{Q_q(\Omega)\,Y_{lm}(\Omega)}\,d\sigma(\Omega)\Bigr),$$
where $Q_q(\Omega)$ denotes the restriction of the polynomial $Q_q$ to $S^2$;

(c) the angular factor vanishes unless $l'=l+1,\ m'=m+q$ or $l\ge1,\ l'=l-1,\ m'=m+q$; these are necessary conditions only: no assertion is made that an allowed pair has nonzero radial integral, and no transition probability is asserted or computed;

(d) for the oscillator: with $\omega>0$, $\ell:=\sqrt{\hbar/(m\omega)}$, the complete orthonormal family $(\psi_n^{\mathrm{osc}})$ of [[thm-nrqm-oscillator-oscillator-scaling-and-exact-realization]] and the position operator $X$ (multiplication by $\ell y$ in the scaled variable) one has
$$X\psi_n^{\mathrm{osc}}=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}\bigl(\sqrt n\,\psi_{n-1}^{\mathrm{osc}}+\sqrt{n+1}\,\psi_{n+1}^{\mathrm{osc}}\bigr),$$
so $\langle\psi_{n'}^{\mathrm{osc}},X\psi_n^{\mathrm{osc}}\rangle$ vanishes unless $n'=n\pm1$, with the displayed coefficients; in particular the oscillator position matrix elements are supported on a single step $|\Delta n|=1$, while the Coulomb selection rules constrain only $\Delta l$ and $\Delta m$ and leave the radial integral free.

This item concerns matrix elements of multiplication operators on $L^2$ and
their finiteness and selection rules; it asserts no absorption, emission or
transition rate and no physical interpretation.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Use the notation of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-harmonic-polynomial-dimension]]: $S^2=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ with polar measure
$\sigma$ ([[lem-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-integral-in-angle-coordinates]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]), the Hilbert space $L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ with inner
product linear in the first argument, the complete orthonormal family $(Y_{lm})$
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-associated-polynomial-normalization]],
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]]), the blocks $V_l=\operatorname{span}\{Y_{l,-l},\dots,Y_{ll}\}$ and
the finite span $H$, the spaces $H_l^{\mathrm{pol}}$ of complex harmonic homogeneous polynomials of degree $l$,
and the polynomial representatives $h_{lm}\in H_l^{\mathrm{pol}}$ of the $Y_{lm}$, characterized by
$\mathrm{res}_l(h_{lm})=Y_{lm}$ where $\mathrm{res}_l(p)$ is the class of $p|_{S^2}$
([[def-homogeneous-polynomial-and-homogeneous-ideal]], [[def-monomials-multidegree-and-total-degree]],
[[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]). Put $H_{-1}^{\mathrm{pol}}:=\{0\}$, fix $l\ge0$ and $m\in\{-l,\dots,l\}$,
write $\mathcal H:=h_{lm}$, and define the three polynomial multipliers
$$Q_0:=x_3,\qquad Q_\pm:=\frac{x_1\pm ix_2}{\sqrt2},$$
so that $Q_q=\sum_{i=1}^3c_{q,i}x_i$ with $c_{0,i}=\delta_{i3}$ and $c_{\pm,i}=(\delta_{i1}\pm
i\,\delta_{i2})/\sqrt2$. Let $D_i$ and $L_z,L_3$ be as in
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]], where $L_3=L_z$ and $L_zY_{lm}=\hbar mY_{lm}$
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-laplacian-diagonal-domain]]). Then, for each $q\in\{-1,0,1\}$:

(a) (harmonic decomposition) the polynomial $G_q:=\dfrac{\sum_ic_{q,i}\,\partial_i\mathcal H}{2l+1}$ lies in
$H_{l-1}^{\mathrm{pol}}$ and
$$Q_q\,\mathcal H=R_q+r^2G_q,\qquad R_q:=Q_q\mathcal H-r^2G_q\in H_{l+1}^{\mathrm{pol}},$$
where $r^2(x)=x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2$; for $l=0$ one has $G_q=0$ and $R_q=Q_q\mathcal H$;

(b) (degree selection) the function $Q_q|_{S^2}\cdot Y_{lm}$ lies in $V_{l+1}\oplus V_{l-1}$ (with
$V_{-1}:=\{0\}$); consequently, for all $l'\ge0$ and $m'\in\{-l',\dots,l'\}$,
$$\langle Q_q|_{S^2}\,Y_{lm},\ Y_{l'm'}\rangle=0\qquad\text{whenever } l'\notin\{l-1,\,l+1\};$$

(c) (weight selection) as elements of $H\subset L^2(S^2,\sigma)$ one has
$$L_z\bigl(Q_q|_{S^2}\,Y_{lm}\bigr)=\hbar(m+q)\,\bigl(Q_q|_{S^2}\,Y_{lm}\bigr),$$
because $\partial_\varphi Q_q=iq\,Q_q$ on $S^2$ ([[def-sine-and-cosine-by-power-series]],
[[def-complex-exponential]]); hence in addition
$$\langle Q_q|_{S^2}\,Y_{lm},\ Y_{l'm'}\rangle=0\qquad\text{whenever } m'\ne m+q;$$

(d) (selection rules) combining (b) and (c): the angular matrix element
$\langle Y_{l'm'},\,Q_q|_{S^2}\,Y_{lm}\rangle$ can be nonzero only if
$$l'=l+1\ \text{and } m'=m+q,\qquad\text{or}\qquad l\ge1,\ l'=l-1\ \text{and } m'=m+q;$$
in particular only $\Delta l=\pm1$ and $\Delta m\in\{0,\pm1\}$ occur with the component-dependent shift
$\Delta m=q$ for the multiplier $Q_q$. These are necessary conditions on the angular integrals only: no
assertion is made that an allowed pair has a nonzero integral, and no absorption, emission or transition
probability is asserted or computed.

Adopt the framework data and the declared perturbed-family model of
[[def-nrqm-approximations-framework-perturbed-family-model]] in the
**simple-label case**: $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$, $V=V^{*}\in
\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ with $v=\|V\|>0$, $H(\lambda)=H_{0}+\lambda V$ on
$D(H_{0})$ for real $\lambda$, and $E$ is an isolated eigenvalue of $H_{0}$ of
**multiplicity one** with gap at least $g>0$,
$\operatorname{dist}(E,\sigma(H_{0})\setminus\{E\})\ge g$. Let $\psi_{0}$ be a
normalized eigenvector, $P_{0}\psi_{0}=\psi_{0}$, let
$$S:=\iota_{Q_{0}}\bigl(H_{0}|_{D(H_{0})\cap Q_{0}\mathfrak H}-E\bigr)^{-1}Q_{0}, \qquad Q_{0}=I-P_{0},$$
be the reduced inverse of the model clause (c)(iii), and put
$$R:=\frac{g}{8v}.$$
Then for every real $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|<R$:

(a) $H(\lambda)$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$; the model's followed label
$E_{\lambda}$ of the contour $|z-E|=g/2$ exists, is the unique spectral value
of $H(\lambda)$ inside that contour, is real, and its spectral projection is
the orthogonal rank-one projection
$P_{\lambda}=E_{H(\lambda)}(\{E_{\lambda}\})$;

(b) the gauge-fixed eigenvector
$$\psi(\lambda):=\frac{P_{\lambda}\psi_{0}}{\langle P_{\lambda}\psi_{0},\psi_{0}\rangle}$$
is analytic in $\lambda$, satisfies $\langle\psi(\lambda),\psi_{0}\rangle=1$
and $(H_{0}+\lambda V)\psi(\lambda)=E_{\lambda}\psi(\lambda)$, and
$$q:=2|\lambda|v/g\le\tfrac14,\qquad \|P_{\lambda}-P_{0}\|\le\tfrac13,\qquad \|\psi(\lambda)\|\le2 ;$$

(c) the model's label identity
$$E_{\lambda}=\bigl\langle (H_{0}+\lambda V)\psi(\lambda),\psi_{0}\bigr\rangle =E+\lambda\langle V\psi(\lambda),\psi_{0}\rangle$$
holds, so the deviation $\lambda\mapsto E_{\lambda}-E$ of the model's energy
label is controlled by the perturbation alone;

(d) the exact coefficients are
$$E'(0)=\langle V\psi_{0},\psi_{0}\rangle,\qquad \psi'(0)=-SV\psi_{0},\qquad E''(0)=-2\langle VSV\psi_{0},\psi_{0}\rangle,$$
with $|E'(0)|\le v$, $\|\psi'(0)\|\le v/g$ and $|E''(0)|\le2v^{2}/g$; the
second-order coefficient involves the whole complementary spectral subspace of
$H_{0}$ through $S$, continuum included;

(e) the cubic remainder obeys
$$\left|E_{\lambda}-E-\lambda E'(0)-\frac{\lambda^{2}}{2}E''(0)\right| \le \frac{Rv\,(|\lambda|/R)^{3}}{1-|\lambda|/R},$$
so at $|\lambda|=R/2$ the bound is $g/32$ and for $|\lambda|\le R/2$ it is at
most $128v^{3}|\lambda|^{3}/g^{2}$;

(f) if $v=0$, that is $V=0$, then $P_{\lambda}=P_{0}$, $E_{\lambda}=E$ and
$\psi(\lambda)=\psi_{0}$ for every real $\lambda$, and no radius involving
division by $v$ is used in this branch;

(g) the theorem is conditional on the strict positive gap, on the multiplicity
one of $E$ and on the boundedness of $V$; it asserts no unbounded or
degenerate perturbation theorem, no time-dependent perturbation, and no
statement about which branch of the family a preparation occupies.

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt P1, P2 and P4
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) for a declared system, with the
state, sharp-observable and evolution readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable

suppliers.

**(b) The perturbed family.** As an additional model assumption of the pair,
fix a self-adjoint operator $H_{0}:D(H_{0})\subseteq\mathfrak H\to\mathfrak H$
on the declared state space, **declare** $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$ to be the
unperturbed sharp energy observable,
fix a bounded self-adjoint operator $V\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]) with
$$v:=\|V\|<\infty$$
([[def-operator-norm]]) and fix a real **coupling** $\lambda$ (dimensionless:
$\lambda V$ is read in joules). Declare the **perturbed family**
$$H(\lambda):=H_{0}+\lambda V,\qquad D(H(\lambda)):=D(H_{0}),$$

$H_{0}$-bounded with $H_{0}$-bound $0\le a<1$ (the bound inequality holds with

([[thm-kato-rellich]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).

**(c) The gapped label.** Fix an isolated eigenvalue $E\in\mathbb R$ of $H_{0}$
of finite multiplicity $r\ge1$ with gap
$$\operatorname{dist}\bigl(E,\sigma(H_{0})\setminus\{E\}\bigr)\ge g>0,$$
and put $P_{0}:=E_{H_{0}}(\{E\})$ and $Q_{0}:=I-P_{0}$
([[def-discrete-and-essential-spectrum-of-a-self-adjoint-operator]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]],
[[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]]). The
definitions used by the pair are those of the cited suppliers:

(i) for real $\lambda$ with $|\lambda|v<g$, the **followed perturbed label**
$E_{\lambda}$ is the spectral value of $H(\lambda)$ inside the counterclockwise
circle $|z-E|=g/2$, and $P_{\lambda}$ is its Riesz projection of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-contour-perturbation-projection]] clause (b); for
such $\lambda$ the label is unique and $P_{\lambda}$ is the orthogonal spectral
projection of $H(\lambda)$ at $E_{\lambda}$; at $\lambda=0$ one has
$E_{0}=E$ and $P_{0}$ as displayed;

(ii) the **first-order operator** is the Hermitian operator
$$V_{E}:=\bigl(P_{0}VP_{0}\bigr)\big|_{P_{0}\mathfrak H}$$
on the finite-dimensional eigenspace $P_{0}\mathfrak H$, whose spectrum
$\operatorname{spec}(V_{E})\subseteq[-v,v]$ is the model's first-order shift
data (joules per unit coupling);

(iii) the **complementary reduced inverse**
$$S:=\iota_{Q_{0}}\bigl(H_{0}|_{D(H_{0})\cap Q_{0}\mathfrak H}-E\bigr)^{-1}Q_{0}$$
is the bounded operator of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-simple-level-reduced-resolvent-coefficients]]
when $r=1$, and the analogous bounded reduced inverse $B(z)$ of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-degenerate-feshbach-error]] clause (a) for
general $r$; its role is to record that the **whole** complementary spectral
subspace, continuum included, contributes to the second-order data.

**(d) Scope.** Clauses (a)-(c) cover bounded perturbations of a self-adjoint
operator and a fixed isolated finite-multiplicity label only. The definition
asserts no time-dependent perturbation, no adiabatic ramping of $\lambda$, no
statement that a preparation occupies the branch of $E_{\lambda}$ or of any
eigenvalue of $V_{E}$, no branch-population or relaxation statement, no
measurement and no identification of the model with a laboratory system; the
labels $E_{\lambda}$ are spectral data of the declared family.

derivations.claim: [The compressed matrices] By [L2], each $D^{W}_{j}$ is a compression of a self-adjoint operator to $W$, hence a Hermitian $2\times2$ matrix with unit $\mathrm{C\,m}$; the diagonal entries $\langle\psi_{1},D_{j}\psi_{1}\rangle$ and $\langle\psi_{2},D_{j}\psi_{2}\rangle$ factor into a radial integral times an angular integral with $l'=l$, which vanishes by the selection rule; and the off-diagonal entries factor with angular labels $(l,m)=(0,0)$, $(l',m')=(1,0)$, for which only the component $q=0$, that is $D_{3}$, can contribute. Choosing the phase of $\psi_{2}$ so that the surviving number is real and positive gives $D^{W}_{1}=D^{W}_{2}=0$ and $D^{W}_{3}=D_{\rm rel}\sigma_{1}$ with $D_{\rm rel}=|\langle\psi_{2},D_{3}\psi_{1}\rangle|>0$, to be read as a model parameter. This is clause (a).

[The two-state family] In the orthonormal basis $(\psi_{1},\psi_{2})$ one has $\Pi_{W}H_{\kappa}|_{W}=\operatorname{diag}(E_{1},E_{2})$ by [L1] and orthogonality of distinct eigenstates; with $v:=D_{\rm rel}(1\ \mathrm{V\, m^{-1}})$ in joules one has $V=-v\sigma_{1}$ and $$H_{S}=\begin{pmatrix}E_{1}&-v\lambda\\-v\lambda&E_{2}\end{pmatrix}.$$ Since $\sigma_{1}$ is Hermitian with $\|\sigma_{1}\|=1$, $V$ is bounded self-adjoint with norm $v$; the exact eigenvalues of a matrix $\begin{pmatrix}a&w\\w&b\end{pmatrix}$ with real $w$ are $\frac{a+b}{2}\pm\sqrt{(\frac{a-b}{2})^{2}+w^{2}}$, verified by the same direct eigenvector computation as in the two-level example of this page with $g:=\Delta$, $w:=-v\lambda$; substituting $a=E_{1},b=E_{2}$ gives clause (b).

[Coefficients] The label $E=E_{1}$ is simple with gap $\Delta$ (the second level is $E_{2}=E_{1}+\Delta$ and there are no further levels in the two-dimensional model); the perturbation $V$ is bounded self-adjoint with norm $v$; hence [L3] applies for $|\lambda|v<\Delta/8$. Since $V$ has vanishing diagonal, $E'(0)=\langle V\psi_{1},\psi_{1}\rangle=0$.
